reviews.review_text:
flyingphd
Singapore, Singapore5 contributions
0
Food was good but not worth the price tag; customer service was bad overall
Sep 2025 • Solo
I had been to Yuzu before and the last time it was a great experience. I booked dinner today for their special 2nd anniversary called "Hoi" (in collaboration with Mua Sake) and expected a great treat, but it turned out to be a disaster for various reasons.

- Food (which is the most important in my book) - Good but the quantity was fairly disappointing. The price tag is higher than usual, but both the quantity and quality were lower than usual. The combination of Vietnamese and Japanese cuisine was creative, but I am not sure if it justifies the price tag.
- Services - This is where things went wrong, on so many dimensions (and if you're Vietnamese/ work in Vietnam, do read on). 
 - Delay - I was rushing to arrive on time, only to be told that the dinner would be delayed by 10-15 mins (which turned out of be a good 20 mins). It would have been ok if the dinner weren't at 8PM and stretched to start at only 8:20-8:30... The restaurant told us to be on time, or else they would reserve the right to refuse entry, but they (a Japanese restaurant) refused to let guests in until 20 mins past the booking time. I was also asked if I wanted any drink while waiting, to which I said yes, and none was brought to be during the 20 minutes...
 - Gift - There was some drinking game during the dinner, which I won, and the gift was supposed to be some lunch voucher. None was given to me, but I didn't bother asking cause I was sure I would not want to return.
 - Tax invoice (for the Vietnamese/ those who work in Vietnam) - When I made the booking and was asked to pay deposit, I was also given the option of getting the red invoice for the deposit amount of VND 5M (~50% of the bill). I asked the staff if I should tick the box, to which I said no need and told me that I could just red the tax invoice after paying for the whole amount after dinner. Guess what, after dinner they refused to issue the invoice because they said they could only issue the invoice up to 5M... I was like WTF... I didn't bother arguing any further, but if they didn't want to issue to the invoice to dodge tax or whatever, they might as well just have said so since the beginning.

All in all, a waste of time, a waste of money. The quality clearly has dropped vs. 1-2 years ago. The only saving grace was the lady chef at the counter, who seemed genuinely nice and wanted the customers to have a good experience. She's the 1 star that I decided to leave for this rating.

Impressive Omakase experience at Yuzu Omakase Viet Nam
Jun 2024 • Friends
At this elegant restaurant in the heart of District 1, you can enjoy omakase menu sets that changes seasonally. Behind the door lies an intimate counter housing 16 prized seats where you will sit right up to the chef’s cutting boards. Inside the restaurant, you’ll see the beautiful yuzu tree, and some dishes is adorned with yuzu accents. 
The 14 piece omakase meal I had was very good. This course captures magical culinary moments, serving some of the seasonal specialties fresh from Japan and non -Japanese ingredients such as wagyu A5, caviar, foie gras, truffle... comes into play. 
Each course was total delight, and chef were expert in explaining each ingredients in each dish, plus the paired Sake. 
Some of the highlights on the menu include Suimika, Kinmedai, Masaba, Amaeri Ebi, Chawan & Truffle, Otoro & Caviar, Bafun Uni Sushi, and Negitoro. The fish is sliced with precision and paired with delicate sauces and garnishes that accentuate the natural flavors. Another standout is wagyu sushi, which is meltingly tender and infused with spices. The desert with sakura jelly was fresh and delicious.
Overall it was a good experience, highly recommend.

Dinner of 16 million for 2 people, is it worth it?
May 2024 • Couples
I've known about this Yuzu Omakase restaurant for a long time, but only now have I had the chance to experience it. 
I booked a table for 2 people and chose the 6.5 million course, plus VAT and drinks, so the bill was about nearly 16 million. This price is the most expensive compared to other Omakase NHs. 
The food is very fresh and delicious, there are unique performances by the chef throughout the meal to help keep the dinner from being boring and customers can also interact and chat with the chef. What I like about the restaurant is that there is a Sommelier who advises and recommends wine to customers because I am someone who likes to drink wine on special occasions or on dates, but I don't know much about wine, so I really need Sommeliers who can. Advise and help me choose a bottle of wine that is delicious and suitable for me. 
Overall, I feel that spending a large amount of money on a date dinner for 16 million is quite satisfying, the food is delicious, the chef and service are both very cute and enthusiastic. 
I rate 8/10 for food and service. The remaining 2 minus points for the restaurant location are quite difficult to find because it is a one-way street and if you overtake, you have to turn around quite far. The next minus point is that even though I spent more than tens of millions of money, I still have to sit with friends. Other guests and the chef served not only the 2 of us but also 3 other guests. When we came to eat, the room was full so it was quite noisy, for guests who need privacy and don't like crowded noisy places. You should not book the main room but can choose a private room.

- Omakase style menu helps diners have new and creative culinary experiences, as the chef freely combines ingredients.

I watched a lot of review clips on Tiktok, I really liked it, but looking at the price, I was a bit shocked. But in the end, I still decided to experience it with two friends. We used the set for 4 million/person, with about 18 dishes, including dessert. You really get what you pay for, all the dishes are delicious. My favorite dish is Bafun Uni Sushi. It's soft and fatty. The chef also adds a lot of Uni. I'm so addicted.
We ate 18 dishes in 2 hours but the chef served the dishes in a very timely manner so we didn't feel overwhelmed or overwhelmed. The chef also takes care and we often ask if we need to adjust the amount of rice or wasabi to get the best taste. Looking at the picture, I thought each dish was very small, but after eating that set, I was very full. After eating, you will also receive a free cake to take home.
The restaurant space is luxurious but quite small, so the waiting area is not comfortable. The day we went, we had to wait about 10 minutes (even though we booked a table in advance) because it was a bit crowded.
